g1.label: 1. Enslaved people worked on ___
g1.why: The text says enslaved African people were forced to work on plantations.

g2.label: 2. The South's economy depended on ___ labour
g2.why: The text says the South's economy depended on unpaid labour.

g3.label: 3. The North had already ___ slavery
g3.why: The text says the northern states had already abolished slavery.

g4.label: 4. Lincoln was against the ___ of slavery
g4.why: The text says Lincoln was against the spread of slavery.

g5.label: 5. Eleven states decided to ___ the US
g5.why: The text says eleven southern states decided to leave the United States.

g6.label: 6. The Civil War began in ___
g6.why: The text says the Civil War began in 1861.

g7.label: 7. Lincoln issued the ___ Proclamation
g7.why: The text says Lincoln issued the Emancipation Proclamation in 1863.

g8.label: 8. The war ended with victory for the ___ states
g8.why: The text says the war ended in 1865 with victory for the northern states.

g1.label: 1. Millions of people ___ forced to work as slaves
g1.why: A state true before the war (a later reference point) uses the past perfect passive.

g2.label: 2. When Lincoln ___ elected...
g2.why: ‘When’ + a single completed event uses the simple past passive.

g3.label: 3. The North had already ___ slavery
g3.why: This completes the past perfect ‘had already abolished’ with the past participle.

g4.label: 4. By 1865, the northern states ___ the war
g4.why: ‘By 1865’ signals an action completed by that past point, so the past perfect is used.

g5.label: 5. The war ___ four long years
g5.why: A simple statement of duration uses the simple past: ‘lasted’.

g6.label: 6. By the time the Proclamation was issued, the war ___ begun
g6.why: ‘By the time’ signals an action completed before another past point, so the past perfect is used.

g7.label: 7. Although they ___ their freedom...
g7.why: An action completed before the main clause's past time uses the past perfect.

g8.label: 8. Slavery ___ abolished in 1865
g8.why: ‘In 1865’ is a specific past time, so the simple past passive ‘was’ is used.

g1.label: 1. When the war ___ (start)
g1.why: ‘When’ + a single event uses the simple past, contrasting with the ongoing past perfect continuous background.

g2.label: 2. By 1860, the North ___ (turn)
g2.why: ‘By 1860’ signals an action completed by that point, so the past perfect is used.

g3.label: 3. Lincoln ___ the election in 1860 (win)
g3.why: A specific past year takes the simple past: ‘won’.

g4.label: 4. The states left after Lincoln ___ president (become)
g4.why: ‘After’ + past perfect shows one action completed before another past action.

g5.label: 5. The war ___ four years (last)
g5.why: A simple statement of duration uses the simple past: ‘lasted’.

g6.label: 6. They were free because Lincoln ___ the Proclamation (sign)
g6.why: The cause (signing) happened before the result (being free), so the past perfect is used.

g7.label: 7. Slavery ___ abolished in 1865 (be)
g7.why: ‘In 1865’ is a specific past time, so the simple past ‘was’ is used.

g8.label: 8. Although they ___ freedom (gain)
g8.why: An action completed before the main clause's past time uses the past perfect.
